procedural_history.originating_court: High Court of Gujarat at Ahmedabad
procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Order dated 16.04.2015 of the High Court of Gujarat at Ahmedabad in Criminal Appeal Nos. 477 and 478 of 2000.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The High Court of Gujarat at Ahmedabad delivered a Judgment and Order on 16.04.2015 in Criminal Appeal Nos. 477 and 478 of 2000.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The Supreme Court heard Criminal Appeal Nos. 895-896/2018, and delivered a judgment on 17.07.2018. Subsequently, Miscellaneous Application No. 2597 of 2018 was filed by accused no. 2/respondent no. 1 seeking modification of the judgment dated 17.07.2018, specifically regarding the statement that he was a Government servant. The Supreme Court modified its earlier judgment, convicting the accused under Section 8 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, and reducing the sentence from one year to six months.

decision.conviction_status: The conviction of the accused no. 2/respondent no. 1 under Sections 7 and 13(1)(d) read with 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 is modified as the conviction under Section 8 of the said Act
decision.sentence_status: the sentence of one year imposed is reduced to six months

issue.issue_text: Whether the conviction of the accused no. 2 under Sections 7 and 13(1)(d) read with 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, should be modified on the ground that he was not a public servant.

facts: The accused no. 2 filed a petition to modify a prior judgment which had incorrectly stated that he was a government servant.
The bribe amount, in currency notes, was recovered directly from the accused no. 2.
Signs of anthracene powder, used in trap cases, were found on the shirt pocket of the accused no. 2.
law: Sections 7 and 13(1)(d) read with 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, pertain to offenses committed by a public servant.

Section 8 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, pertains to the offense of taking gratification, by corrupt or illegal means, to influence a public servant, and can apply to a person who is not a public servant.
application: The Court acknowledged the factual error that the accused no. 2 was not a government servant.
Because he was not a public servant, the Court determined that a conviction under Sections 7 and 13 was inappropriate.
However, the Court found that the evidence, specifically the recovery of the bribe money from the accused, was sufficient to establish the ingredients of an offense under Section 8 of the Act.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court accepted the petition and modified the judgment. It changed the conviction of accused no. 2 from Sections 7 and 13(1)(d) read with 13(2) to a conviction under Section 8 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988. Consequently, the Court also reduced his sentence from one year to six months.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the conviction of the accused no. 2 under Sections 7 and 13(1)(d) read with 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, should be modified on the ground that he was not a public servant.
appellant_arguments: The text does not mention any arguments made by the appellant in response to the respondent's application for modification.
respondent_arguments: The respondent (accused no. 2) argued that the judgment should be modified because it incorrectly stated that he was a Government servant, which was factually wrong.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: The recovery of a bribe amount from a person who is not a public servant is sufficient to establish the ingredients for a conviction under Section 8 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: Although the accused no. 2 was not a Government servant, making a conviction under Sections 7 and 13 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, incorrect, the evidence proved that the bribe money was recovered directly from him. This factual finding establishes the necessary ingredients for an offense under Section 8 of the Act, which applies to non-public servants, thereby justifying a modification of the conviction to that section.
legal_tests_applied: The court assessed whether the evidence on record, specifically the recovery of bribe money (currency notes) and the presence of anthracene powder on the accused's shirt, satisfied the ingredients of Section 8 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
why_appellant_lost: The original conviction under Sections 7 and 13(1)(d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, was based on the factually incorrect premise that the accused no. 2 was a Government servant.
why_respondent_won: The respondent successfully demonstrated that the original judgment contained a material factual error, as he was not a Government servant, which is a necessary element for an offense under Sections 7 and 13 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
